mainTopic: Repaying debts in שביעית, a lender's claim of a lost פרוזבול, and the status of a captured slave who was redeemed
overview: In the שמיטה year a lender must tell a borrower who repays 'I cancel it.' If the borrower answers 'Even so,' the lender may take the money. רבה adds that the lender may look on hopefully while he waits, and the גמרא tells how רבה's own borrower missed his cue until אביי taught him. Next, רב נחמן rules that a lender is believed if he says he had a פרוזבול and lost it, since nobody skips the easy permitted way. רב would even prompt lenders to make that claim. A משנה seems to disagree, and the גמרא answers that this is a debate among תנאים. A new משנה then asks about a captured slave who was redeemed: does he stay a slave? אביי explains the case as before the owner gave up hope, and רבא explains it as after, and each gives his own reason for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The גמרא then asks how the redeemer can own the slave at all, and ריש לקיש begins proving from a פסוק that a גוי can own another גוי's labor, a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Repaying a debt in the Sabbatical Year
steps.stepSummary: A borrower who repays during שביעית must first hear the lender say 'I cancel it.' If the borrower then says 'Even so,' the lender may take the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone pays back a debt in שביעית, the lender must say 'I cancel it.' If the borrower answers 'Even so,' the lender may accept it, because the פסוק says 'And this is the matter of the cancellation.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the base ruling of the משנה that the whole passage is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיטה cancels the debt, so the lender may not simply collect it. He must first announce that he cancels it. After that, the borrower is free to give the money anyway, and the lender may take it. The source is the word 'דְּבַר' in the פסוק, which can also mean 'speech,' teaching that the cancellation must be said out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year (שמיטה), when loans are cancelled

steps.whatToRemember: There are two steps: the lender says 'מְשַׁמֵּט אֲנִי,' then the borrower says 'אַף עַל פִּי כֵן,' and only then may the lender take the money.

phrases.english: One who repays a debt to his fellow in the Sabbatical Year –
he (the lender) must say to him: 'I cancel it';

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״אַף עַל פִּי כֵן״,
phrases.english: and if he (the borrower) said to him: 'Even so,'
he may accept it from him.
As it says: 'And this is the matter of the cancellation.'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:2. The word דְּבַר can also mean 'speech,' so the lender has to say the cancellation out loud.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender must declare 'I cancel it'; if the borrower insists 'Even so,' the lender may accept payment.

steps.title: The lender may look on hopefully
steps.stepSummary: רבה adds that the lender may show, by looking at the borrower hopefully, that he would like the borrower to say 'Even so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The lender may 'hang his eyes' on the borrower, hoping, until the borrower says 'Even so.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds a detail to the משנה: the lender does not have to act completely uninterested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once the lender says 'I cancel it,' he must stay totally passive. רבה says he may hint with his look that he wants the money. The only requirement is that the borrower is the one who says the words 'Even so.'

keyTerms.meaning: He 'hangs' on him, meaning he looks at him hopefully

phrases.english: Rabba said:
And he may hang [his eyes] on him until he says this.
phrases.notes: 'Hang' here means the lender keeps looking at him hopefully, hinting that he wants to be paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: וְתָלֵי לֵיהּ עַד דְּאָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a permission to the משנה's procedure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender may show he hopes to be paid until the borrower says 'Even so.'

steps.title: The borrower should call it a gift
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: the borrower should not say 'I am paying my debt' but 'It is mine, and I give it to you as a gift.' This seems to make the payment entirely the borrower's own idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: When the borrower gives it, he should not say 'I am paying my debt.' He should say 'It is mine, and I am giving it to you as a gift!'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה with a ברייתא that seems to require the payment to come completely from the borrower's own initiative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower must present the money as his own free gift, it seems the lender should not be pushing or hinting at all. That appears to conflict with רבה's permission to look on hopefully.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to him (from a teaching)

phrases.english: Abaye objected to him:
When he (the borrower) gives it to him,

phrases.aramaic: אַל יֹאמַר לוֹ: ״בְּחוֹבִי אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לָךְ״,
phrases.english: he should not say to him: 'I am giving this to you as payment of my debt,'
rather he should say to him:
'It is mine, and I am giving it to you as a gift!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's statement
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the lender may look on hopefully
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires the money to be given as a free gift from the borrower, which seems to leave no room for the lender to encourage it.

steps.title: The lender may hope for that too
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the lender may also look on hopefully until the borrower says the gift wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: He may look on hopefully for that too, until the borrower says this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי by applying his same rule to the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only tells us which words the borrower must say. It does not forbid the lender from hoping. So the lender may hint until the borrower says 'It is a gift,' just as he may hint until the borrower says 'Even so.'
steps.whatToRemember: What matters is the words the borrower says. The lender's hopeful look is allowed in both cases.

phrases.english: He (Rabba) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: תָּלֵי לֵיהּ נָמֵי עַד דְּאָמַר הָכִי.
phrases.english: He may also hang [his eyes] on him until he says this.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the gift wording from the ברייתא: 'It is mine, and I give it as a gift.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תָּלֵי לֵיהּ נָמֵי עַד דְּאָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the same rule to the new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gift wording means the lender must stay completely passive
steps.terutzMaskana: The lender may hope and hint until the borrower says the gift wording

steps.title: רבה's borrower takes the money home
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא owed רבה money and brought it in שביעית. רבה said 'I cancel it,' and the borrower simply took the money and left.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא בר מרתא, also called אבא בר מניומי, owed רבה money. He brought it to him in שביעית. רבה said 'I cancel it.' He took the money and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that shows the rule of the משנה in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה did his part by saying 'I cancel it.' But the borrower did not know he was supposed to answer 'Even so,' so he took the words at face value and went home with the money.

phrases.english: Abba bar Marta,
who is Abba bar Minyumi,
Rabba was owed money by him.
He brought it to him in the Sabbatical Year;
he (Rabba) said to him: 'I cancel it.'
He took it and left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא בַּר מָרְתָּא, דְּהוּא אַבָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the משנה's procedure in action
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender said 'I cancel it,' and the borrower did not answer 'Even so.'

steps.title: אביי finds רבה sad
steps.stepSummary: אביי finds רבה sad and asks why. רבה tells him what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי came and found him sad. He asked: Why is the Master sad? רבה told him: This is what happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues and sets up אביי's visit to the borrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה was upset because he had followed the rule correctly, yet lost his money. The borrower simply did not know his part. This sets up אביי stepping in.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Master,' a respectful way to address a rabbi

phrases.english: Abaye came,
he found him that he was sad,
he said to him: Why is the Master sad?
He said to him: This is what happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה explains the incident to אביי.

steps.title: אביי questions the borrower
steps.stepSummary: אביי goes to אבא בר מרתא and confirms that רבה said 'I cancel it' and that the borrower never answered 'Even so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי went to him and asked: Did you bring the money to the Master? Yes. What did he say to you? 'I cancel it.' Did you say 'Even so'? No.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions the borrower step by step to find out where things went wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through his questions, אביי finds the missing piece. The borrower skipped the second half of the procedure: answering 'Even so.'

phrases.english: He went to him,
phrases.notes: אביי went to the borrower, אבא בר מרתא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמְטֵית לֵיהּ זוּזֵי לְמָר?
phrases.english: he said to him: Did you bring the money to the Master?
He said to him: Yes.
He said to him: And what did he say to you?
He said to him: 'I cancel it.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וַאֲמַרְתְּ לֵיהּ ״אַף עַל פִּי כֵן״?
phrases.english: He said to him: And did you say to him 'Even so'?
He said to him: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל לְגַבֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמְטֵית לֵיהּ זוּזֵי לְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי investigates the incident
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the borrower answered 'Even so' after רבה said 'I cancel it'

steps.title: אביי tells him to go back
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that had he said 'Even so,' רבה would have taken the money. He tells him to bring it now and say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If you had said 'Even so,' he would have taken it from you. Now, at least, bring it to him and say 'Even so.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי teaches the borrower his missing part and tells him to fix it now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי explains that רבה's 'I cancel it' was not a refusal. It was only the first step of the procedure. It is not too late, so the borrower can return and complete it.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, at least / in any event

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאִי אֲמַרְתְּ לֵיהּ ״אַף עַל פִּי כֵן״,
phrases.english: He said to him: And if you had said to him 'Even so,'
he would have taken it from you;
now, at least, bring it to him,
and say to him 'Even so.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אֲמַרְתְּ לֵיהּ אַף עַל פִּי כֵן, הֲוָה שַׁקְלִינְהוּ מִינָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי acts on what he found out
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Saying 'Even so' would have allowed רבה to accept the money, so the borrower should go back and say it.

steps.title: The borrower returns and רבה accepts
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא brings the money back, says 'Even so,' and רבה takes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went, brought it to him, and said 'Even so.' רבה took it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows the procedure being completed correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower said 'Even so,' רבה was allowed to accept the payment, exactly as the משנה rules. The story confirms the two-step procedure in practice.

phrases.english: He went and brought it to him,
and said to him 'Even so.'
He (Rabba) took it from him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The borrower follows אביי's advice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the borrower said 'Even so,' רבה accepted payment.

steps.title: רבה's remark about the young scholar
steps.stepSummary: רבה remarks that this young תלמיד חכם had not understood the procedure from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This young Torah scholar did not have the understanding from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבה's comment on why things went wrong the first time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה explains that the problem was the borrower's lack of knowledge, not the law. He should have known on his own to answer 'Even so,' and instead he had to be taught.
steps.whatToRemember: The lender's 'מְשַׁמֵּט אֲנִי' is not a real refusal. A knowledgeable borrower is expected to answer 'אַף עַל פִּי כֵן,' and then the lender may take the money.

phrases.english: He said: There was no understanding in him,
in this young Torah scholar, from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲוָה בֵּיהּ דַּעְתָּא בְּהַאי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing comment on the story
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The procedure works when the borrower knows to say 'Even so.' The first failure came from the borrower's lack of knowledge.

steps.title: A lender is believed to say he lost his פרוזבול
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב נחמן: a person is believed when he says he had a פרוזבול and lost it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב נחמן: A person is believed if he says, 'I had a פרוזבול, and I lost it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. A lender who cannot show a פרוזבול is still believed if he says he had one and lost it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a loan is canceled after שמיטה unless the lender wrote a פרוזבול. Here the lender has no document to show, but רב נחמן says his word is enough and he may collect.

keyTerms.meaning: A document a lender gives over to בית דין so that שמיטה does not cancel his loans

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Naḥman said:
A person is believed to say:
"I had a prosbol in my hand,
phrases.notes: A פרוזבול keeps a loan alive past שמיטה. Without one, the debt would be canceled.

phrases.english: and it got lost from me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the פרוזבול after the story of רבה and the canceled debt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender is believed to claim he had a פרוזבול that was lost, and he may collect.

steps.title: Why he is believed: nobody gives up the permitted way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason. Since the חכמים made the פרוזבול easy to get, a person would not skip it and collect in a forbidden way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since the חכמים set up the פרוזבול, a person would not leave the permitted way and 'eat' the forbidden way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we believe the lender, and then gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing a פרוזבול is easy and available to anyone. So we assume a lender would simply have written one instead of collecting a canceled debt, which would be forbidden. That assumption is what makes his claim believable.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים set up a rule

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since the Sages set up the prosbol,
a person does not leave the permitted and eat the forbidden.
phrases.notes: "Eat" is just a way of speaking. He means collecting the money in a forbidden way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב נחמן's ruling in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the lender believed without showing a document?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פרוזבול is easy to get, so we assume he would not collect a canceled debt in a forbidden way.

steps.title: רב would prompt the lender to make the claim
steps.stepSummary: When lenders without a פרוזבול came before רב, he would ask them whether they had one that got lost. The גמרא says this counts as 'open your mouth for the mute.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came before רב, he would say to the lender: 'Did you have a פרוזבול, and it got lost?' A case like this is 'open your mouth for the mute.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רב acted in practice. He helped lenders by suggesting the claim to them, and the גמרא explains why that was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a judge may not feed a claim to one side. But since the claim is almost surely true, as step 12 explained, רב is only helping someone who did not know what to say. That is what the פסוק 'open your mouth for the mute' means.

keyTerms.meaning: Open your mouth for the mute: speak up for someone who cannot speak for himself

phrases.english: When they came before Rav,
phrases.notes: 'They' means a lender with no פרוזבול who wanted to collect after שמיטה.

phrases.english: he would say to him: Did you have any prosbol
that you had, and it got lost?
A case like this is "Open your mouth for the mute."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב going even further than רב נחמן by suggesting the claim to the lender.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge may prompt a lender to claim a lost פרוזבול, because this is helping someone who cannot speak for himself.

steps.title: A משנה says a loan without a פרוזבול is not collected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a lender who brings a loan document without a פרוזבול cannot collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: And likewise, a lender who brings out a loan document and has no פרוזבול with it, these debts are not collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן and רב with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the lender has no פרוזבול in hand, he loses the debt. It does not say we believe him if he claims he lost one. That seems to clash with the rule that he is believed.

phrases.english: We learned: And likewise, a lender
who brings out a loan document,
and has no prosbol with him –
these are not paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rulings of steps 11 and 13 from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that a lender is believed to say he lost his פרוזבול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a lender without a פרוזבול in hand does not collect, so his word alone should not be enough.

steps.title: It is a debate among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תנאים argue about this. One view requires a פרוזבול, and the חכמים say it is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a debate among תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: One who brings out a loan document must have a פרוזבול with him. And the חכמים say: He does not need one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the משנה follows only one side of a debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא records two opinions. The first matches the משנה and requires a פרוזבול. The חכמים say it is not needed, and רב נחמן and רב follow them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a debate among תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן and רב hold that a lender is believed to say he lost his פרוזבול. The משנה that says otherwise follows the first opinion in the ברייתא, while they follow the חכמים.

phrases.english: It is a debate of tanna'im –
as it is taught: One who brings out a loan document –
must have a prosbol with him.
And the Sages say: He does not need it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Debate among תנאים: the משנה follows one opinion, and רב נחמן follows the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה looked like the final rule that a lost פרוזבול claim is not accepted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the view that requires a פרוזבול. רב נחמן follows the חכמים, who do not require one.

steps.title: The new משנה: a captured slave who was redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a redeemed captive slave stays a slave if he was redeemed as a slave, and goes free if he was redeemed as a free man. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he stays a slave either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A slave was captured, and people redeemed him. If they redeemed him as a slave, he stays a slave. If they redeemed him as a free man, he does not stay a slave. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: either way, he stays a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה opens a new topic: an עבד who was taken captive and then bought back by others. Two opinions are given about whether he is still a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא makes it depend on the redeemer's intent, "as a slave" or "as a free man." רבן שמעון בן גמליאל ignores that difference and says he is always still a slave. The משנה does not say whose slave he becomes, and the גמרא will fill that in.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish (Canaanite) slave owned by a Jew
They redeemed him (paid ransom to free him)
For the purpose of being a free man

phrases.english: MISHNAH
A slave who was captured, and they redeemed him,
phrases.notes: "They" means other Jews, not his own master.

phrases.english: if they redeemed him as a slave, he is enslaved;

phrases.aramaic: אִם לְשׁוּם בֶּן חוֹרִין – לֹא יִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד.
phrases.english: if they redeemed him as a free man, he is not enslaved.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Either way, he is enslaved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, unrelated to the פרוזבול discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the outcome follows the redeemer's intent (as a slave = enslaved, as a free man = free). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: he is enslaved in every case.

steps.title: Before or after the owner gave up hope? Neither fits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the משנה means. Before יאוש, he should never go free. After יאוש, he should never stay a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What case are we talking about? If you say it is before the owner gave up hope, then even if he was redeemed as a free man, why would he not be a slave? But if it is after the owner gave up hope, then even if he was redeemed as a slave, why would he be a slave?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out what case the משנה is describing. It shows that both obvious options seem to clash with the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יאוש, the slave still belongs to his first master, so the redeemer's intent to free him should not matter. After יאוש, the slave becomes ownerless and goes free by himself, so the redeemer's intent to keep him a slave should not matter either. Either way, the תנא קמא's distinction seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing?
The owner giving up hope of getting his property back

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about how he was redeemed. It is about timing: did the redemption happen before or after the original master gave up hope? Each timing option breaks one half of the משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA
With what case are we dealing?
If you say it is before the owner gave up hope,

phrases.aramaic: לְשׁוּם בֶּן חוֹרִין – אַמַּאי לָא יִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד?
phrases.english: then if redeemed as a free man, why would he not be enslaved?
Rather, say it is after the owner gave up hope,
then if redeemed as a slave, why would he be enslaved?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case setting of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's distinction between being redeemed as a slave and being redeemed as a free man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma. Before יאוש, ownership stays with the first master no matter what. After יאוש, the slave is automatically free no matter what. So the redeemer's intent should never matter.

steps.title: אביי: it is before the owner gave up hope
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה is talking about before יאוש. Redeemed as a slave, he goes back to his first master. Redeemed as a free man, he belongs to no one, so that people will not stop redeeming captives.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, the case is before the owner gave up hope. If he was redeemed as a slave, he is a slave to his first master. If he was redeemed as a free man, he is not a slave to the first master or to the second master. He is not a slave to the second master, because that man redeemed him as a free man. He is not a slave to the first master either, because otherwise people might hold back and not redeem slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the dilemma. He picks the "before יאוש" option and explains why a slave redeemed as a free man still goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly speaking, the slave still belongs to the first master. However, the חכמים freed him when he is redeemed as a free man, as a safeguard. If redeemers knew that he would just go back to his old master, they would not bother to redeem him. The second master has no claim either, because he himself chose to redeem him as a free man.

keyTerms.meaning: His second master (the one who redeemed him)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a rabbinic rule that overrides normal ownership in order to protect the important practice of redeeming captives.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Actually, it is before the owner gave up hope,
and if redeemed as a slave, he is enslaved to his first master;
if redeemed as a free man, he is not enslaved

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְרַבּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא לְרַבּוֹ שֵׁנִי;
phrases.english: not to his first master and not to his second master.
Not to his second master,
because he redeemed him as a free man;
and not to his first master either,
lest people hold back and not redeem slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 17 by choosing the before-יאוש case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case (before יאוש) and adds a rabbinic reason that explains the free-man ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Before יאוש, the slave must go back to his first master no matter how he was redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before יאוש, the slave goes free if he was redeemed as a free man, because the חכמים did not want people to stop redeeming captives.

steps.title: Why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he stays a slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: redeeming slaves is a מצוה just like redeeming free people, so there is no worry that people will stop doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: either way, he is a slave. He holds that just as it is a מצוה to redeem free people, so too it is a מצוה to redeem slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words from the משנה, this time to explain his reasoning within אביי's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא freed the slave out of fear that people would stop redeeming slaves. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that redeeming slaves is itself a מצוה, so people will redeem them anyway. Without that fear, the slave simply returns to his first master as normal ownership requires.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a commandment to redeem captives

steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's reading, both opinions in the משנה are talking about before יאוש. The argument is only whether people would stop redeeming slaves. The תנא קמא worries they would, so a slave redeemed as a free man goes free. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says redeeming slaves is a מצוה too, so he always returns to his first master.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Either way, he is enslaved,
phrases.notes: He means enslaved to the first master, since it is still before giving up hope.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּצְוָה לִפְדּוֹת אֶת בְּנֵי חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: because he holds: just as it is a מצוה to redeem free people,
so too it is a מצוה to redeem slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּצְוָה לִפְדּוֹת אֶת בְּנֵי חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's explanation by giving the reason behind the second opinion in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the disagreement in the משנה as a dispute over whether people will hold back from redeeming slaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sees no reason for the safeguard, because redeeming slaves is a מצוה. So the slave always returns to his first master.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה is talking about after the owner gave up hope
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the first opinion of the משנה as a case after יאוש. Redeemed as a slave, he belongs to the redeemer. Redeemed as a free man, he belongs to no one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה is really talking about after the first master gave up hope. If he was redeemed as a slave, he becomes the slave of his second master, the one who redeemed him. If he was redeemed as a free man, he is not a slave to the first master or the second. Not to the second, because the second redeemed him as a free man. Not to the first either, because the first master had already given up on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to read the משנה than אביי did. He says the case is after the first master gave up hope of getting his slave back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the case was before יאוש. רבא moves it to after יאוש, so the first master has lost his claim. That answers the question from step 17: after יאוש the slave can stay a slave, but only to the new master who redeemed him as a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to introduce the true reading of a case
Giving up hope; here, the first master gave up on getting his slave back
Redeemed in order to be a slave
Redeemed in order to be a free man
His second master, the person who redeemed him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two masters. The "first master" is the original owner who gave up hope. The "second master" is the one who paid to redeem him from captivity.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Really, it is talking about after the master gave up hope,
and if redeemed as a slave, he is a slave to his second master,
if redeemed as a free man, he is not a slave

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְרַבּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא לְרַבּוֹ שֵׁנִי;
phrases.english: not to his first master and not to his second master;
not to his second master,
because he redeemed him as a free man,
and not to his first master either,
because it was after he gave up hope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 17, different from אביי's answer in steps 18-19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (after יאוש instead of before)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After יאוש the slave could never stay a slave, so the משנה's case seemed impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: After יאוש he can stay a slave to the redeemer if he was redeemed as a slave. Redeemed as a free man, he belongs to no one.

steps.title: רבא explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל using חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling that he stays a slave either way is based on חזקיה's reason. Slaves must not be able to free themselves by handing themselves over to raiding troops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he stays a slave either way. This follows חזקיה, who said: Why did they say he stays a slave either way? So that every slave will not go and hand himself over to raiding troops and in that way get himself out of his master's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now explains the second opinion in the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, according to his own reading. He uses a reason given by חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading the first opinion is not worried that people will stop redeeming captives. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason cannot be about that. Instead it is a rule to stop slaves from escaping: if being captured set a slave free, slaves would let themselves be captured on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose reason רבא uses here
Troops / raiding bands that take captives
Takes himself out of someone's ownership

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the challenge that follows. רבא's reason for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (חזקיה's) is different from אביי's reason (redeeming slaves is a מצוה too).

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
either way, he stays a slave –
this follows Chizkiyya,
as Chizkiyya said:
For what reason did they say
that either way he stays a slave?
So that it will not be that each and every slave
goes and hands himself over to raiding troops,
and gets himself out of his master's hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד – כִּדְחִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reading. Having explained the first opinion, he now explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a reason for the second opinion that fits the new reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבא's first opinion is not worried about people stopping to redeem, it is unclear why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל keeps him a slave to stop slaves from freeing themselves through capture, as חזקיה said.

steps.title: A ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying "just as", which fits אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. There, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says redeeming slaves is a מצוה just like redeeming free people. This wording fits אביי's reading well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to them: Just as it is a מצוה to redeem free people, so it is a מצוה to redeem slaves. This works well for אביי, who said the case is before יאוש. That is why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said "just as".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an objection against רבא by quoting a ברייתא. First it shows that the ברייתא fits אביי. This sets up the problem for רבא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the first opinion worries people will stop redeeming slaves. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers that worry with "just as": redeeming slaves is also a מצוה, so people will keep doing it. The words of the ברייתא match אביי's explanation from step 19 exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
To redeem, to buy a captive free
It makes sense for this view, but... (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to them:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּצְוָה לִפְדּוֹת אֶת בְּנֵי חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: Just as it is a מצוה to redeem free people,
so it is a מצוה to redeem slaves.
It makes sense according to Abaye –
who said it is before the master gave up hope,
that is why he said "just as";

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to רבא's explanation in steps 20-21 by quoting a ברייתא that fits אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (step 21)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason as "redeeming slaves is a מצוה too." That matches אביי, not רבא.

steps.title: For רבא, the word "just as" does not fit
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא the case is after יאוש, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is חזקיה's. So why would he say "just as"?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבא, who said the case is after יאוש, is "just as" the reason? His reason is because of חזקיה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its objection. It points out that the ברייתא's wording does not match the reason רבא gave for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the first opinion was never worried about people stopping to redeem slaves. So there is nothing for "just as" to answer. רבא said רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is חזקיה's concern about slaves escaping, but the ברייתא gives a completely different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But (here: but according to the other view)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the case is before יאוש, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is "redeeming slaves is a מצוה too". רבא: the case is after יאוש, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason is חזקיה's (stop slaves from escaping). The ברייתא's word "כשם" fits אביי and challenges רבא.

phrases.english: But according to Rava –
who said it is after the master gave up hope,
is this "just as" the reason?!
It is because of Chizkiyya!
phrases.notes: He means: for רבא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason should be חזקיה's, so "just as" seems out of place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרָבָא – דְּאָמַר לְאַחַר יֵאוּשׁ, הַאי ״כְּשֵׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 22 by showing the ברייתא does not fit רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason follows חזקיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's reason ("just as" it is a מצוה) answers a worry that only exists in אביי's reading. In רבא's reading there is no such worry, and his reason for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is different.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answered both possible cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did not know which case the רבנן meant. 'Just as' is his answer for before יאוש, and חזקיה's reason is his answer for after יאוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say to you: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did not know what the רבנן meant. So he told them: if you mean before יאוש, my reason is 'just as'. If you mean after יאוש, my reason is like חזקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא against the question from Step 23. It explains why the words 'just as' still appear in the ברייתא even according to רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was not sure whether the רבנן were talking about before or after יאוש, so he answered both. 'Just as' (redeeming slaves is a מצוה) covers the case before יאוש. חזקיה's reason covers the case after יאוש, which is the case רבא says the משנה is really about. So the words 'just as' do not disprove רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting his property back
'Just as': here, redeeming slaves is a מצוה just like redeeming free people
The אמורא whose reason is that slaves must not free themselves by handing themselves over to raiders
The Sages, the first opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the משנה is talking about before יאוש. He still holds it is after יאוש. The 'just as' line is only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל covering the other possibility.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא הָוֵי יָדַע
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel did not know
what the Rabbis were saying,
and this is what he said to them:
If you are talking about before the owner's despair,
that is the 'just as' reason;
if you are talking about after the despair,
it is like Chizkiya.
phrases.notes: This is the reason from Step 21: a slave must not be able to free himself by giving himself over to raiders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 23 against רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The speaker was uncertain about the case, so he gave two answers, one for each possible case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'just as' seemed to show that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's whole reason is the מצוה of redemption, which would fit only אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Just as' answers only the before-יאוש case. For after יאוש, which is רבא's case, the reason is חזקיה's.

steps.title: From whom does the second master acquire the slave?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, after יאוש the redeemed slave belongs to his second master. But that master bought him from the gentile captor. Can a captor own a slave at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא, the case is after יאוש, and the slave belongs to his second master. From whom did the second master acquire him? From the captor. But does the captor himself own him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reading from a new direction. It asks how the second master can own the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer can only own what the seller owned. If the gentile captor never really owned the slave, the redeemer could not have gotten ownership from him. That would weaken רבא's claim that the redeemer owns the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: His second master, the one who redeemed him from captivity
A captor, the raider who took the slave
Acquires him, gets ownership of him

phrases.english: And according to Rava, who said the case is after the despair,
and the slave belongs to his second master;
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 20: if he was redeemed as a slave, he belongs to the one who redeemed him.

phrases.english: the second master, from whom did he acquire him?
From the captor.
Does the captor himself own him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא survives the wording question, the גמרא raises a new legal problem with his reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (Step 20) that after יאוש the slave redeemed as a slave belongs to the redeemer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ownership passes only from someone who has it. A gentile captor seems to have no ownership, so the redeemer could not get any from him.

steps.title: A gentile can own another gentile for his labor
steps.stepSummary: Yes, the captor does own the slave, for his labor. ריש לקיש learns from a פסוק that a גוי can acquire another גוי for his labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, the captor owns him for his labor. ריש לקיש said: How do we know that a גוי can acquire another גוי for his labor? Because the פסוק says, 'And also from the children of the residents who live with you, from them you shall acquire.' You acquire from them,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the captor does have ownership over the slave's labor. It starts bringing ריש לקיש's source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that a captor owns the slave for his labor. The redeemer can then get that ownership from him. ריש לקיש begins reading the פסוק closely: 'you acquire from them.' How this proves that a גוי can acquire another גוי is spelled out in his next words, which continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: His labor, literally 'the work of his hands'
The אמורא who brings the source from the פסוק
Residents, non-Jews living among the Jews

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבא's reading. The second master's ownership rests on real ownership that the captor had.

phrases.english: Yes; he owns him for his labor,
as Reish Lakish said:
From where do we know that a gentile can acquire a gentile
for his labor?
As it is said:
"And also from the children of the residents
who live with you, from them you shall acquire"
you acquire from them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the kind of ownership: the captor owns the slave's labor, and this is backed by a פסוק through ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A gentile captor has no ownership at all, so the redeemer cannot acquire from him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי can acquire another גוי for his labor, so the captor had real ownership to pass on to the redeemer.
